title: DC-area forecast: Staying very humid tonight, then hotter Thursday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: It's a soupy evening with temperatures in the 70s and an isolated shower possible.

What’s next? Staying humid and turning hotter tomorrow through the weekend. Shower and storm chances continue, mainly during the afternoons into evenings.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: An isolated shower possible this evening, then partly cloudy to mostly clear overnight. Staying super muggy with lows in the low to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): Partly sunny and hotter with highs heading for the upper 80s and low 90s most spots. Continued high humidity (dew points still in low to mid-70s) helps the heat index peak in the upper 90s to near 100. The chance of isolated to scattered showers and storms is mainly after 3 or 4 p.m. and especially from near DC and I-95 to the west. With the higher heat, some storms could be strong to severe with localized flooding and damaging winds. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Isolated to scattered showers and storms, a few with potential to be strong to severe, remain possible during the evening. Partly cloudy and muggy overnight with lower rain chances and lows in the 70s. Confidence: Medium

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The weather pattern is pretty much stuck Friday through Sunday. Highs should be in the upper 80s to mid-90s, and it's still quite humid with dew points mainly in the low 70s. Late-day isolated to scattered showers and storms are possible each day, although chances may be lower on Sunday. Muggy nighttime lows are around 70 to 75. Confidence: Low-Medium

Similar heat and humidity look to stick around Monday and Tuesday. A chance for showers and storms may linger as well, with Tuesday perhaps having the higher chance.

DC weather history for August 5

Blistering heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 102 degrees amid a devastating drought, part of a summer that saw a record number of 100-degree days and severe agricultural losses.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: The heat holds back, but humidity makes a comeback, and we're dodging some showers and storms with a flood risk. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
